headline: IDF not planning Oct 10 Iran strike. US congressional nominee Brad Lander detained with 90 West Bank olive-harvest volunteers
dek: Opposition leaders escalate warnings against pre-election military escalation; Eisenkot rules out Netanyahu-led coalition.
fault_line: Is the Iran-war drumbeat before Oct 27 about security — or about Netanyahu's survival?

sections.what_happened: Opposition leaders escalate warnings against pre-election military escalation; Eisenkot rules out Netanyahu-led coalition.
sections.what_verified: Haaretz live updates; consistent with 1400-02 item.
sections.what_disputed: Netanyahu camp denies election-driven war planning (per 1400 window).
sections.why_matters: Israel votes in six days and the opposition's warning is now on record: no intelligence reason to attack Iran now, says Lapid — while Katz announces a new security zone on live TV.
sections.context: Background: Israel elections Oct 27 — Eisenkot vows to resign rather than join a Netanyahu-led government (Haaretz); Yair Golan urges IDF to block any pre-election military action serving Netanyahu (Haaretz); Lapid repeats no intel reason to attack Iran now (covered 1400-02); JPost: IDF not planning Oct 10 Iran strike. US congressional nominee Brad Lander detained with 90 West Bank olive-harvest volunteers (Al-Monitor/JPost).

totw_analysis: Our read: Israel votes in six days and the opposition's warning is now on record: no intelligence reason to attack Iran now, says Lapid — while Katz announces a new security zone on live TV. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is the Iran-war drumbeat before Oct 27 about security — or about Netanyahu's survival?
